text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Constitutional Court rejected a government decision to sack deputy interior minister General Agim Shehu, making clear high ranking officers can only be dissmissed by President Sali Berisha.
- Lushnje residents in southern Albania threatened they would not allow President Sali Berisha to visit their town.
- Socialist Party supporters in Vlore want party leader Fatos Nano to campaign in their town, a symbol of anti-Berisha rebellion.
- Parliament speaker Pjeter Arbnori turned down a request by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to summon parliament to lift the state of emergency.

- Hundreds of people threw flowers into the sea in Vlore on Wednesday to mark 60 days since more than 100 people drowned after a ship carrying Albanians collided with an Italian navy frigate and sunk.
ALBANIA

- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum urged Albania's political parties to take part in the parliamentary elections, saying the word boycott should be removed from the Albanian vocabulary.
- King Leka, seeking support for the restoration of the monarchy, had a successful visit to the northern district of Mirdite.
- Two people were killed and seven injured in a shoot-out between rival gangs in the southern town of Berat.
- The Democratic League of Kosovo bitterly attacked Serbian authorities, saying they had staged poltically-motivated trials to persecute ethnic Albanians.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- An Albanian politician claims that Democratic Republic of the Congo leader Laurent Kabila was a student in Albania in 1964. He was called Pol Kobongo.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Pole of Liberty, the Italian rightest alliance, vowed to back the Democratic Party in the upcoming elections, Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu said after a visit to Italy.
- The central bank has intervened to halt further devaluation of the currency lek. On Tuesday, the U.S dollar was quoted at 190 leks, up from 165 last week.
INDIPENDENT
- Democratic Alliance Party leaders accused Prime Minister Bashkim Fino of being President Sali Berisha's ally and warned they would quit from the national reconciliation government.
- Thousands of people welcomed Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano in the port town of Durres, chanting anti-Berisha slogans.
